hints: The kth row from the top is n-k XOR steps above the bottom.
A value after t steps is the XOR of entries whose offsets are submasks of t.
Apply one XOR shift for each set bit of t to compute all requested positions together.
analogy: Each set bit in the number of levels doubles the pattern of contributing bottom entries at that offset.
example: For bottom [1,2,3] and k=2, one step gives [1 XOR 2, 2 XOR 3]=[3,1].
algorithm: Let t=n-k. For every set bit b of t, update a[i] to a[i] XOR a[i+2^b] for i increasing from 0 while the second index exists. After all selected shifts, print the first k values.
correctness: Over XOR, (1+z)^t factors into the product of (1+z^(2^b)) over set bits of t. Each pass applies one factor, so the resulting entry is exactly the value after t pyramid steps.
complexity: For n values, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
